Name: Login and Registration 1
Description: Plate 4.2 displays the application’s landing screen, login page, and account registration page. The landing screen presents a “Start learning” button, a login option, an overview of the Lessons, Practice, and Quiz learning loop, and a progress summary stored on the device. The login page accepts an email or username and a password, and provides remember-me, forgot-password, registration, and backup-restore options. The registration page collects the full name, username, email, password, password confirmation, a security question and answer, and agreement to the Terms and Conditions.

Name: Home Dashboard 1
Description: Plate 4.3 shows the home dashboard, which gives users an overview of their learning status. It presents the user’s greeting, total experience points (XP), current level, daily streak, daily signing goal, and a “Continue where you left off” card linking to the most recent activity. It also shows summary statistics for signs passed, drill attempts, quizzes completed, and modules completed, together with a badge preview and an energy indicator. A guided tour tooltip with the application mascot appears on the first screen.

Name: Practice Sign Demonstration 1
Description: Plate 4.5 illustrates the sign demonstration page, which presents a reference video of a sign, in this case “Hello,” with playback, replay, and speed controls. The page also shows the sign’s category tags, a short description, step-by-step practice instructions, and the “Mark as learned” and “Start Practice” buttons. The third screen shows the camera view used to record the user’s own performance of the sign, with a recording timer and an on-screen prompt.

Name: Camera-guided Assessment 1
Description: Plate 4.6 shows the camera-guided assessment workflow, in which the user records a sign for evaluation. The first screen displays a framing guide with the instruction to keep the head, shoulders, and hand in view, along with the record button and lighting and camera controls. The succeeding screens allow the user to trim the recorded clip, retake it, or confirm it for submission, followed by a review dialog that indicates the clip is being analyzed. The preview areas appear black in the screenshots.

Name: Assessment Outcome and Frog-Mascot Feedback 1
Description: Plate 4.7 presents the outcome-based feedback interface displayed after camera-guided assessment. Instead of presenting a numerical recognition score, FSLAMES communicates the result as Correct, Needs correction—try again, or Couldn't read clearly—recapture. The frog mascot reinforces the outcome through concise and encouraging guidance, while sign-specific feedback helps the learner determine whether to continue, review the demonstration, repeat the attempt, or recapture the sign under improved camera conditions.
